items.name: PRA Model Risk Management (SS1/23)
items.description: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23: model risk management principles for banks, building societies and PRA-designated investment firms, including models built with AI and machine-learning techniques

requirements.text: Every model used in prudential decision-making sits in a firm-wide, documented model inventory - including models built with AI or machine-learning techniques, in-house or third-party - with risk-based tiering by materiality and complexity driving validation effort.
requirements.rationale: Tiering keeps validation proportionate; unlisted models are ungoverned risk.

controls.description: Maintain the firm-wide model inventory with materiality and complexity tiering applied to AI/ML models.
Identify and classify new or changed models, including third-party AI, before prudential use.

requirements.text: The board exercises oversight of model risk, approves the model governance framework and ensures adequate resources for model risk management; firms maintain clear ownership and accountability for AI/ML models used in prudentially relevant activities.
requirements.rationale: SS1/23 places ultimate responsibility for model risk with the governing body.

controls.description: Report model risk profile, material model exceptions and framework changes to the board at least annually.

requirements.text: AI/ML models undergo independent validation and verification, with documented evidence of model performance, limitations and appropriateness for purpose.
requirements.rationale: Independence is the check that developer optimism does not become firm risk.

controls.description: Validate models independently of their developers before deployment and on change, recording performance, limitations and suitability.
Keep development documentation sufficient for an independent reviewer to reproduce model behaviour.

requirements.text: Models are assessed on their impact on business outcomes and tested under stress scenarios to evaluate resilience, with mitigants and controls documented for identified model risk.
requirements.rationale: Outcome-focused testing surfaces model failure modes that input-focused validation misses.

controls.description: Stress-test material models and document outcome impacts, mitigants and contingency actions.
